\chapter{Communication Complexity — Func Hash}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem.FuncHash
\section{Overview}

This module establishes a key probabilistic lemma for Newman's theorem: a uniformly
random hash function $h : \alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k$ collides on any two distinct
inputs with probability at most $1/k$.  The argument proceeds by decomposing the
collision event into $k$ pairwise-disjoint pieces, measuring each piece, and summing.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Hash function space]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.HashSpace}
\leanok
$\texttt{HashSpace}\,\alpha\,k$ is the type of all functions $\alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k$,
i.e.\ the space of hash functions on $\alpha$ with output range $\{0,\dots,k-1\}$.
Equipped with the product probability measure (uniform over each coordinate), it serves
as the ambient probability space for the random-hash argument.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Collision piece]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.HashSpace}
For $x, y : \alpha$ and $a : \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, $\texttt{collisionPiece}\,k\,x\,y\,a$ is
the set of hash functions $h \in \texttt{HashSpace}\,\alpha\,k$ satisfying $h(x) = a$ and
$h(y) = a$, i.e.\ the subset of the product space where both $x$ and $y$ are mapped to
the fixed value $a$.  These pieces partition the collision event $\{h \mid h(x) = h(y)\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Collision event as union of pieces]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collision_mem_iUnion}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.HashSpace, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece}
\difficulty{4}
For any $x, y : \alpha$ and any $k$,
\[
  \{h : \texttt{HashSpace}\,\alpha\,k \mid h(x) = h(y)\}
  \;=\; \bigcup_{a : \mathrm{Fin}\,k} \texttt{collisionPiece}\,k\,x\,y\,a.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Collision pieces are pairwise disjoint]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece_pairwiseDisjoint}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece}
\difficulty{3}
For any $x, y : \alpha$ and $k$, the sets $\texttt{collisionPiece}\,k\,x\,y\,a$ for
$a : \mathrm{Fin}\,k$ are pairwise disjoint: if $a \ne b$ then
$\texttt{collisionPiece}\,k\,x\,y\,a \cap \texttt{collisionPiece}\,k\,x\,y\,b = \emptyset$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Singleton measure in hash range]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.hashRange_singleton_measure}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For $k \ge 1$ and any $a : \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, the uniform measure of the singleton
$\{a\} \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,k$ equals $1/k$ as an extended non-negative real:
$\mu(\{a\}) = 1/k \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^\infty$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Singleton measure in hash range (real-valued)]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.hashRange_singleton_measureReal}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.hashRange_singleton_measure}
\difficulty{3}
For $k \ge 1$ and any $a : \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, the real-valued uniform measure of $\{a\}$
in $\mathrm{Fin}\,k$ equals $1/k \in \mathbb{R}$, i.e.\ $\mu_{\mathbb{R}}(\{a\}) = 1/k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Measure of a collision piece]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece_measureReal}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.measureReal_pi_univ, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.hashRange_singleton_measureReal}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, $k \ge 1$, $x \ne y \in \alpha$, and $a : \mathrm{Fin}\,k$.
Under the product measure on $\texttt{HashSpace}\,\alpha\,k$,
\[
  \mu_{\mathbb{R}}(\texttt{collisionPiece}\,k\,x\,y\,a) = \left(\frac{1}{k}\right)^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Collision probability bound]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collision_prob_le}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.measureReal_iUnion_fintype, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.HashSpace, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece_measureReal, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece_pairwiseDisjoint, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collision_mem_iUnion}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, $k \ge 1$, and let $x \ne y \in \alpha$.
For a uniformly random hash function $h : \alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k$,
\[
  \Pr[h(x) = h(y)] \;\le\; \frac{1}{k}.
\]
That is, $\mu_{\mathbb{R}}\bigl(\{h \in \texttt{HashSpace}\,\alpha\,k \mid h(x) = h(y)\}\bigr) \le 1/k$.
\end{theorem}
